title: Factors and multiples
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: List all the factors
sections.objective: Find every factor of a number, without missing any.
explain: A factor divides the number evenly. Every factor pair is a way to make a rectangle.
Factors are never bigger than the number: 48 is a multiple of 24, not a factor.

visual.caption: Every rectangle you can make with 24 squares is a factor pair.

sections.key: Factors come in pairs that multiply to the number. Try 1, 2, 3, … and stop when the pairs start repeating.

sections.title: Prime factorization
sections.objective: Write a number as a product of primes.
explain: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 are prime. 1 is not prime, and neither is 9 (3 × 3).
Type the primes one at a time with Next. The order doesn't matter.
sections.key: Keep splitting into factors until every number is prime. A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
sections.workedCaption: Tap through: split until everything is prime.

sections.title: Greatest common factor
sections.objective: Find the biggest number that divides two numbers evenly.
explain: You'll use it to simplify fractions in one step: 24/36 ÷ 12/12 = 2/3.
sections.key: The greatest common factor is the biggest number on both factor lists.

worked.note: The biggest one in both lists.

sections.workedCaption: Tap through: list, then find the biggest match.

sections.title: Least common multiple
sections.objective: Find the smallest number both numbers divide into.
explain: The least common multiple is the smallest number in both lists of multiples.
Multiplying the two numbers always gives a common multiple, but not always the least. It's the same idea as a common denominator.
sections.key: Count by the bigger number and stop at the first one the smaller number divides into.

worked.note: Not 48 (6 × 8): that's a common multiple, but not the least.

sections.workedCaption: Tap through: count by the bigger number.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Factors, prime factorization, GCF and LCM, mixed together.
explain: Now the problems are mixed. Read what each one asks for.
sections.key: Factors divide into a number. Multiples are what you get counting by it. Greatest common factor; least common multiple.

hints.whole.factors-multiples.factors: Go in pairs: 1 × ?, 2 × ?, 3 × ?, ... Stop when the pairs meet.
hints.whole.factors-multiples.primes: Split the number into any two factors. Keep splitting until every number is prime.
hints.whole.factors-multiples.gcf: List the factors of both numbers. Find the biggest one that's in both lists.
hints.whole.factors-multiples.lcm: Count by the bigger number. Stop at the first one the smaller number divides into.
hints.whole.factors-multiples: Read what the problem asks for first: factors, primes, greatest common factor or least common multiple.

misconceptionMessages.whole.multiples-not-factors: Those are multiples (you get them by counting by the number). Factors divide INTO the number, so they're never bigger than it.
misconceptionMessages.whole.factor-pairs-missed: Every number there is a factor, but some are missing. Go in pairs: 1 × ?, 2 × ?, 3 × ?, ...
misconceptionMessages.whole.not-all-prime: The product is right, but not every number is prime yet. Keep splitting the ones that aren't.
misconceptionMessages.whole.gave-lcm: That's a common multiple. The question asks for a common FACTOR: a number that divides into both.
misconceptionMessages.whole.common-not-greatest: That divides both numbers, but there's a bigger one that does too.
misconceptionMessages.whole.gave-gcf: That divides into both numbers. The question asks for a common MULTIPLE: a number both divide into.
misconceptionMessages.whole.product-not-least: That is a common multiple, but there's a smaller one. Count by the bigger number and stop at the first one that works.
